newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end at new unofficial record.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end at new unofficial record.

text.p: Mexican stocks were well ahead of previous records at the close of trade on Tuesday.
Dealers and analysts said the bourse was advanced further into record territory on a moderate but steady flow of foreign buyers.
Preliminary figures showed the leading IPC share index was up 37.32 points when the closing bell rang, or 0.73 percent, at 5,172.56.

The bourse also showed little reaction to the day's rise in U.S. long bond yields, analysts added, as they were still relatively low and not taken to herald a rise in U.S. base rates at the Aug. 19 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Financial group Bancomer accounted for the lion's share of dealing after news the firm had reached a deal to sell tourist venues worth $133 million, dealers said.
Bancomer B shares gained 14 centavos to 5.74 pesos, while the cheaper A series climbed 48 centavos to 3.90 pesos. The two series accounted for more than 30 percent of all shares traded.
Dealers noted construction and cement firms gained strongly, boosted by speculation that the government was planning to restructure debts for companies holding highway concessions.
Construction firm Empresas ICA Sociedad Controladora gained 45 centavos to 25.20, and cement maker Cemex climbed 70 centavos to 42.25 pesos.
Dealers said gains by Bancomer and the construction companies outweighed profit-taking on market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico, which shed 10 centavos to end at 21.65 pesos.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced decliners by 75 to 37, out of 126 stocks that changed hands.
